name: OEM-light makers Germany
description: M37: German medtech makers classified by production model. D1 OEM-light (target), D2 OEM-heavy, C unclear maker, D not a maker. Writes klass_oem only; the ambulatory klass is never touched.

classification.target_description: German maker that sells medical (or lab) products under its own brand or as private label, with production outsourced or limited to assembly, configuration, labelling and testing (OEM-light). Own development plus own production (OEM-heavy) is not a target.

class_definitions.D1: OEM-light (target): sells medical products under its own brand or as private label for others; production outsourced or limited to assembly, configuration, labelling, testing; signals: Konfektionierung, Montage, Systemintegration, Lieferanten, Partner, Import, Inverkehrbringer, Eigenmarke, Private Label, OEM for third parties, products built around bought-in components (PCs, displays, power, enclosures, sets).
class_definitions.D2: OEM-heavy: own development and own production; signals: Fertigung, Produktion, Werk, CNC, Spritzguss, Reinraum, Made in Germany as a production claim, Werksverkauf, machine park, Tuttlingen instrument forge, more than roughly 100 staff where stated on the site.
class_definitions.C: Medtech maker, the text does not show the production model. Treated as D1 for enrichment (bias rule).
class_definitions.D: Not a maker or out of market: distributor, service company, dental, pharma, software, non-medtech.

classification.rule: Assign D2 only when the text states own production or a plant: eigene Fertigung or Produktion described as the company's own (Werk, Produktionshalle, machine park, CNC, Spritzguss, Reinraum production, 'wir produzieren selbst', all production steps in house, Made in Germany as a production claim). Contract manufacturing (Lohnfertigung) or OEM production for other brands on the company's own machines (Drehen, Fräsen, Schweißen, CNC, laser) is own production: D2, even when the company also sells its own brand. Private label or OEM for third parties counts as D1 only when the production itself is bought in or limited to assembly. A generic word like Fertigung in a quality or mission sentence, CNC or plants at suppliers, and assembly, kitting (Konfektionierung), set packing, labelling or testing (even in own clean rooms) are not D2: they are D1. Everything else that makes or brands a medical product is D1 or C. When in doubt between D1 and D2, choose D1 or C, never D2. Staff and revenue per head are not required; staff stated on the site is one signal only. Use D only for companies that do not make or brand medical or lab products.
